text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

In a move which will streamline a wide range of corporate regulations, including laws governing capital raising, takeovers, securities trading and directors' duties, the Howard Government is planning a wide-ranging review of Australia's corporate law over the next two years in a bid to cut red tape for business. Page 1.

Under a proposal being considered by the Federal Government taskforce formed to resolve issues involved in the High Court's controversial Wik decision, legislation would define the activities allowed on pastoral leases for farmers and native title-holders The plan could break the deadlock between the hardline stances taken by Aboriginal, State and industry representatives. Page 1.

Speaking on Radio 2LM in Lismore on Friday, Federal Opposition Leader Kim Beazley said the Opposition has backed protection for the sugar industry and the car industry and said its new policy direction is an attempt to put political pressure on the Coaliton to abandon its support for tariff reductions. Page 3.

Market forecasters lifted their estimates of economic growth for the last three months of 1996 by up to 0.3 percentage points after figures released yesterday by the Australian Bureau of Statistics showed business continued to run up inventory levels in te September quarter. Page 3.

THE AUSTRALIAN Amid claims he rorted the Government's travel claims system, embattled Senator Mal Colston will move today that all travelling allowances paid to present and former senators since January 1992 be tabled in the Senate by March 18. The move will mean the travel claims of all senators over the past five years will be open to public scrutiny. Page 1.

In a move that would result in the continuation of the joint Federal and State funding arrangements, the Federal Government looks set to sign fresh legal aid arrangements with Queensland, South Australia, the Northern Territory and the Australian Capital Territory after putting more money on the table. Page 1.

The Queensland Government yesterday launched a A$300,000 advertising campaign, called Please Don't Forget to Protect, which aims to increase parents' awareness of immunisation schedules and inform them of the danger of not immunising. The campaign hopes to lift the level of childhood immunisation from 48 per cent to 95 per cent within five years. Page 1.

Following suggestions by two High Court judges, Justice Sir Daryl Dawson and Justice Michael McHugh, that Victoria's attempted challenge to the 1994 political speech decisions in the Theophanous and Stephens cases might not succeed without an attack on the reasoning of the foundation 1992 cases, Victoria might have to make a more fundamental assault on the constitutional doctrine protecting political speech than the State had so far proposed. Page 3.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

In a day of damning evidence at the New South Wales Police Royal Commission, Department of School Education bureaucrats were forced to admit that a number of teachers were allowed to resign and were given references allowing them to teach interstate or inprivate schools while facing allegations of sexual assault on children as young as five. Page 1.

Rockdale Project A - a proposed Darling Harbour-style entertainment and sporting complex on the shores of the Cooks River, opposite Sydney Airport's international terminal, has reignited anger among aircraft noise groups, which claim it represents a de-facto expansion of the airport and is a setback to the development of a second airport. Page 1.

Following heavy share trading in Bougainville Copper Ltd, ahead of media reports on the decision to use mercenaries to kill or capture leaders of the Bougainville Revolutionary Army, opposition groups in Papua New Guinea are requesting a royal commission into share dealings in Australia linked to the use of the mercenaries on the island. Page 1.

In a bid to speed up the 18-month timetable set by the Federal Government for cutting awards, employers have launched an aggressive push to strip workers' entitlements to a bare minimum with a test case which seeks to eradicate dozens of entitlements suchas rest breaks, protective clothing, health notifications and wage payment details. Page 1.
THE AGE

Following the latest police shooting in Victoria on Sunday night - the State's first in 15 months - police commissioner Neil Comrie yesterday defended Project Beacon, the programme that trained police in ways to avoid shooting when apprehending suspects, an promised a thorough investigation of the shooting. Page 1.

It is believed that, as part of a restructuring of ANZ Bank's cost-laden Australian and New Zealand retail banks, about 700 staff will lose their jobs today when ANZ announces cuts at its finance company subsidiary, Esanda. David Wilson, the bank's head of media relations, said any changes will would be communicated to staff first. Page 1.

Following suggestions from German racing driver Michael Schumacher - a two-time winner of the Formula One world championship - that there is "nothing special" about the Albert Park Grand Prix, Australian Grand Prix Corporation chairman Ron Walker has lashd out at Schumacher's manhood and accused him of being afraid of this year's favourite, Jacques Villeneuve. Page 1.

After running for less than a month at the Princess Theatre, the musical Chess, which stars Barbara Dickson, Daryl Braithwaite and Derek Mertzger and is reported to have cost A$3 million to mount, will close on Saturday week because of poor ticket sales. The producers had hoped the show would run until at least April. Page 1.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373 1800
